fields.title: 📖 Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq: Separate the judgment on the state and on individuals
fields.body:
🖋️ **Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq** distinguished between the outward state of a land and the judgment upon specific individuals.

He explained in meaning: When Shirk becomes visible in a land, forbidden things are practiced openly, and the marks of the religion are set aside, then the outward state of that land is judged severely. At the same time he made clear that there may be individuals within it about whom one does not pass a blanket inward judgment, such as the weak or those who are excused.

🌙 **Conclusion:** This statement concerns the **outward state** and the general classification of visible Shirk and of laws that contradict it. It is not a call to action and not a blanket individual Takfīr upon every person. Judgments upon individuals remain bound to conditions, impediments, and a clear establishment of proof.

immutable.source: 📝 Ḥamad ibn ʿAtīq, in: ad-Durar as-Saniyyah fī l-Ajwibah an-Najdiyyah, Teil 12, Tābiʿ Kitāb Mukhtaṣarāt ar-Rudūd, S. 471.
